work: Dianovics Varga Bognar Aczel - Acceptance and publication lags in scholarly journals 2016-2025
year: 2025 (OSF reg 2025-11-30; Lifecycle Journal v1 2025-12-12; evaluation complete 2026-04; MetaROR assessment+2 reviews 2026-04-29)
type: Research plan (not preregistered; analyses already partly run)
evidence_level_read: Full text of Research Plan docx and OSF registration metadata read; MetaROR assessment/reviews NOT readable (login wall)
research_question: How have acceptance/publication lags changed and what drives them
limitations: Random split; article-level point prediction; PubMed only; declared exploratory with Level-0 prior data access
overlap_with_project: Partial: article-level prediction of acceptance lag and drift description; project's point that it is not out-of-time is correct
remaining_opportunity: Out-of-time journal-level distributional forecasting and calibration

work: Bjork & Solomon - The publishing delay in scholarly peer-reviewed journals
evidence_level_read: Crossref record only; content taken from project and secondary text (not re-read)
strongest_result: Large between-field differences; within-journal variance large (per project)
overlap_with_project: Variance partition (RQ1) is an update of this

work: Luwel Moed et al - Characteristics of publication delays 2000-2016 (Evaluative Informetrics chapter)
evidence_level_read: Crossref record only; content via Dianovics plan text (secondary)
strongest_result: Receipt-to-acceptance median stagnant ~120 d (as cited by Dianovics plan)
limitations: Not read directly; Elsevier only; pre-2017
overlap_with_project: Cited by Dianovics plan not by project; large-scale drift evidence
remaining_opportunity: Drift relative to forecast error; post-2016 period

work: Hadavand Hamermesh Wilson - Publishing Economics: How Slow? Why Slow?
evidence_level_read: Crossref record only; content via Dianovics plan text (secondary)
research_question: Why economics publishing is slow; author vs editor/referee time
strongest_result: Top-5 economics journals acceptance times at least a year; journals and authors hold manuscript comparable time (as cited)
overlap_with_project: Drift/slowness in a field; project cites Ellison 2002 only

work: Phillips & Horn - Review and Publication Times and Reporting Across Journals on Health Policy
research_question: How do journals report review/publication times
evaluation_protocol: None; reported not compared with actual
strongest_result: Total reported times 35-353 d; 16% report no times; reporting inconsistent
limitations: Reported times not verified against article dates; imputation
overlap_with_project: Directly relevant to publisher-reported vs actual turnaround - but it only audits reporting
remaining_opportunity: Matching reported claims to article-level dates; testing claim reliability

work: Hanson Gomez Barreiro Crosetto Brockington - The strain on scientific publishing
evidence_level_read: Abstract read (arXiv 2309.15884; Crossref); full text blocked (403)
method: Five metrics from scrapes and publisher data incl processing times
strongest_result: Special issues with reduced turnaround drove growth
overlap_with_project: Speed-claims context; non-stationarity at publisher level

work: Himmelstein - The history of publishing delays (blog)
research_question: Trend of acceptance and publication delays
method: Per-journal regression of delay on date
strongest_result: Median acceptance delay ~100 d since 1981; journals split between faster/slower
overlap_with_project: Journal-level drift at scale (non-stationarity); cited in project novelty map only

work: Bilalli Munir Abello - A framework for assessing peer review duration of journals (CS)
evidence_level_read: Crossref record only; Springer blocked; characterisation from project (not verified)
strongest_result: Large differences reported vs computed (per project)
overlap_with_project: Closest to publisher-reported vs article-level; small

work: Sebo et al - publication speed in general medical journals (2019); acceptance and publication times in high-impact general medical journals (2022); primary care vs internal medicine 117 journals (2023)
evidence_level_read: Crossref records only; figures via Dianovics plan text (2016 median acceptance lag 123 d for 18 journals)
overlap_with_project: Factor models of journal-level speed; not in project reference list

work: Petrou - Reading the Leaves of Publishing Speed (Scholarly Kitchen)
research_question: Do speed trends signal quality/capacity problems
dataset: Hindawi dump; PubMed (Frontiers Oncology PLOS ONE)
strongest_result: Frontiers Oncology 77->120 d (2022-24); PLOS ONE peak 221 d then ~180 d
overlap_with_project: Non-stationarity of journal turnaround within 2-3 years - supports drift motivation
remaining_opportunity: Quantified drift vs sampling noise at 800 journals

work: Royle - Hold On Hope: publication lag times at cell biology journals (quantixed)
strongest_result: Lags creeping up at some journals not others; max 3263 d

work: Manusights - Peer Review Timelines by Journal (v2026.2)
strongest_result: Median of journal medians 153 d; median within-journal change +32.5% (+13.8% excl Cell Press); states journal median cannot predict individual paper's wait
overlap_with_project: Explicit statement of the project's thesis without test; drift

research_question: Median submission-to-acceptance by journal; submission planner
strongest_result: Planner uses past medians and a three-in-four point
overlap_with_project: It is the practical use case the project evaluates

work: de Jonge & Kramer - Manuscript submission systems and metadata completeness in Crossref
research_question: Crossref metadata coverage by submission system
strongest_result: Coverage of six elements only (not received/accepted)
limitations: Received/accepted not assessed; Springer Nature excluded
overlap_with_project: Not a Crossref-dates study; context for coverage

work: Herrmannova Pontika Knoth - Do authors deposit on time
evidence_level_read: Abstract only; claim about sparse Crossref accepted field is from a search-engine summary and NOT confirmed
limitations: Abstract does not mention Crossref accepted field
overlap_with_project: Weak evidence on sparsity of Crossref accepted date
